notes: Account PD: PeakWave builds conversational risk-advisory assistants for retail brokers.
Primary ask: dedicated capacity with predictable 95th-ms latency for chat + reranking under bursty trading hours.
Scale concerns: daily burst windows (14:55-15:10) with sustained spike for ~10-20 minutes; need fast scale-up without 2-3 minute cold starts.
Desired SLOs: p95 generation latency <= 120ms (short prompts), p95 end-to-end <= 200ms for chat flows. Throughput target: ~600 QPS at 512-token avg across multiple models during peak.
Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to reserved GPUs if autoscaling behavior is deterministic and warm-pool costs are justified.
Quote from CTO: 'If we can't get predictable p95 during market spikes, the product SLA fails'
Technical requests: warm pools (pre-warmed GPU slots), configurable scale-up policy (aggressive on queue depth), scale-down cooldown >= 10 minutes to avoid churn.
Prefer fallback to smaller quantized variant when primary model is saturated; must preserve latency SLO at 90% of quality.
Queueing behavior: want bounded queue length with backpressure to their app and token-based shedding rules rather than request drop.
SLA negotiation points: credits for p95 misses, maximum maintenance window per quarter, guaranteed reserved GPU count during market hours.
Security: require SSO/SAML + audit logging to be forwarded to their SIEM; KMS integration mandatory for any long-term KV cache storage.
Current internal blocker: procurement needs clearer ARR profile vs reserved GPU tiers (SE to produce cost/latency trade-off matrix).
Support references: two Jira tickets open for initial kernel perf tuning (INF-1729) and VPC peering tests (INF-1794).
requirements_summary: Dedicated capacity POC focusing on autoscaling and capacity management: need deterministic scale-up (<30s target for warm-pool spin-up), warm pools to absorb minute-scale bursts, step-scaling rules tied to queue depth and token-rate, hold minimum reserved GPUs during market hours, and graceful degradation to quantized fallback models. Must surface trace-level latency breakdowns, token accounting for cost, and SLA with latency credits. Security: SSO, SOC2 evidence, KMS + audit logs. Network: VPC peering and private control plane.
